lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach a five-part fused-flower family with a superior 3-locular ovary and 3-valved capsule, then split Phlox, Giliastrum and Ipomopsis by leaf architecture and corolla form.

project_scope.selection_mode: Central Texas project module across Phlox, Giliastrum and Ipomopsis
project_scope.note: All seven project source taxa remain within current accepted Polemoniaceae concepts; Phlox pilosa subsp. riparia remains an accepted infraspecific taxon.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the flower: 5 sepals, a fused 5-lobed corolla, 5 epipetalous stamens and a superior ovary. Confirm with a 3-locular capsule that opens in 3 valves.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly herbs in the project pool; leaves may be opposite or alternate, simple to deeply divided, so leaf arrangement alone is not a family rule.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Flowers usually bisexual and 5-merous; corolla sympetalous, often salverform or tubular; stamens 5 and attached to the corolla tube; ovary superior, usually 3-locular.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Capsule, commonly 3-valved, with few to several seeds.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Use the fused 5-part flower plus 3-part capsule first; use foliage and tube length to get to genus.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: 5-part fused flower → 5 epipetalous stamens → 3-locular ovary/capsule → genus doors
visual_lesson.intro: Polemoniaceae is a good example of why flower architecture beats color: blue gilia, red standing cypress and pink phlox all run on the same five-part, three-carpel plan.

steps.title: 1 · Read the flower in fives
steps.look_for: Five calyx lobes and a fused five-lobed corolla.
steps.why_it_matters: Establishes the family framework across very different flower colors and habits.

steps.title: 2 · Find the five stamens in the tube
steps.look_for: Five stamens attached to the corolla tube rather than standing free from the receptacle.

steps.title: 3 · Confirm the three-part fruit
steps.look_for: Superior 3-locular ovary maturing into a 3-valved capsule.
steps.why_it_matters: Strong reproductive confirmation after the flower fades.

steps.title: 4 · Phlox door
steps.look_for: Mostly opposite simple leaves and a salverform corolla with a slender tube and flat spreading lobes.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates the familiar phlox form from the more divided-leaved genera.

steps.title: 5 · Giliastrum door
steps.look_for: More dissected foliage and small blue-purple gilia-type flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: Creates a fast contrast with simple-leaved Phlox.

steps.title: 6 · Ipomopsis door
steps.look_for: Tall flowering axis with deeply divided foliage and long red tubular flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes the hummingbird-pollinated standing-cypress form memorable without treating it as a separate family pattern.

comparisons.title: Polemoniaceae vs Fouquieriaceae
comparisons.rule: Both are close Ericales relatives with fused tubular flowers and superior ovaries. Fouquieriaceae is woody/spiny with 10–16+ stamens and wing-fringed seeds; Polemoniaceae project plants are herbs with 5 stamens and a 3-valved capsule.

comparisons.title: Polemoniaceae vs Ericaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have fused corollas, but Ericaceae commonly has poricidal anthers; Polemoniaceae uses five ordinary epipetalous stamens and a 3-locular capsule.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not make opposite leaves or one corolla shape mandatory; the project genera vary strongly in foliage and tube length.

genera.fast_cue: simple mostly opposite leaves + salverform 5-lobed flower
tall spike-like flowering axis + deeply divided leaves + long red tube

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted; subsp. riparia is also accepted.

show three chambers and opening valves
